newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-Taiwan GDRs fall on valuation doubts.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-Taiwan GDRs fall on valuation doubts.

text.p: Taiwanese global depository receipts dropped in brisk trading Thursday, as wary investors booked gains after the local market hit a seven-year intraday high, traders said.
The Taiwanese rally has been fuelled by massive local liquidity, traders said, and foreign investors are beginning to look sceptically at valuations.
"The volume is absolutely huge," a trader said. "The volatility, volume and valuations all feel a bit frothy."
Selling was concentrated in electronics shares.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index finished 2.42 points lower at 137.13, representing a discount to the local market of 1.78 percent.
Taiwan's share index gained 27.24 points to end at 9,889.45.
Trading in Indian GDRs was thin, with most volume intra-dealer, traders said.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 1.04 points higher at 84.87, an 1.24 percent rise, with the premium over the local market at 19.90 percent from 18.36 percent.
Reliance gained 23 cents to $21.38/$22.13 and Hindalco rose $1.25 to $32.00/$33.00.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index gained 0.35 points firmer, rising to 75.16 points, a premium of 44.25 percent over the local market.
